hero.subheadline: Architecture students design communities for urban, suburban, rural life
hero.valueProposition: The only UIA-endorsed annual student architecture competition in mainland China offers an RMB 80,000 first prize for community design across urban, suburban, or rural living.

content.whyJoin:
The UIA-HYP CUP is the only UIA-endorsed international student architecture competition held annually in mainland China, and 2026 marks its 15th consecutive edition. Organized by Tianjin University, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, and Urban Environment Design (UED) Magazine, it gives architecture students worldwide a platform to work on contemporary architectural, urban, and environmental questions.

This year's topic, Villagers: Urban, Suburban, Rural, is set by Jury Chairman Philip Cox, founding partner of Cox Architecture. Students choose one of three ways of living and propose how relevant, self-sufficient, and sustainable communities can be created, integrating passive energy technologies into the architecture itself. It is a chance to respond to real questions about identity, belonging, and community in a changing world.

The prize pool is substantial for a student competition: RMB 80,000 for first place, RMB 15,000 for five second-prize teams, and RMB 8,000 for twelve third-prize teams, with honorable mentions receiving certificates. Registration and participation are free of charge, and advisors of prize-winning projects also receive certificates.
content.whoShouldApply:
This competition is for architecture and related-major students worldwide, including full-time undergraduates, master's students, PhD students, and students graduating in 2026. Individual entries and teams are both accepted, with up to 4 members and up to 2 academic advisors per team.

It suits students who want to tackle a contemporary community design question in a judged international competition, with a clear brief across urban, suburban, or rural living. It requires the ability to prepare an architectural proposal with relevant submission materials and to register before the September deadline, with final designs due in October 2026.

faq.question: Who can participate?
faq.answer: The competition is open to architecture and related-major students worldwide, including full-time undergraduates, master's students, PhD students, and students graduating in 2026. Individual or team entries are accepted, with up to 4 members and up to 2 academic advisors per team.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee?
faq.answer: Participation is free of charge and open to architecture students worldwide. Registration and submission carry no fee for international entrants.

faq.question: What is the competition topic for 2026?
faq.answer: Under the overarching theme Architecture in Transformation, the 2026 topic is Villagers: Urban, Suburban, Rural. Students select one of three ways of living and propose how communities can be created that are relevant, self-sufficient, and sustainable.

faq.question: What are the prizes?
faq.answer: The first prize is RMB 80,000 and a certificate. Five second-prize teams receive RMB 15,000 each, twelve third-prize teams receive RMB 8,000 each, and several honorable mentions receive certificates. Advisors of prize-winning projects also receive certificates.

faq.question: What are the key deadlines?
faq.answer: Registration closes September 20, 2026 at 24:00 Beijing time. The Q&A deadline is September 30, 2026, and the submission deadline is October 10, 2026 at 24:00 Beijing time. The jury review takes place in November 2026.

faq.question: How is the competition evaluated?
faq.answer: The evaluation consists of a preliminary online review followed by a final review by the international jury panel chaired by architect Philip Cox, who also set this year's topic.

submissionGuide.detail: Read the official brief and topic description for Villagers: Urban, Suburban, Rural on the competition website at hypcup.uedmagazine.net, and check the submission requirements and format rules.
Assemble a team of up to 4 architecture or related-major students, with up to 2 academic advisors. Individual entries are also accepted.
Complete registration by September 20, 2026 at 24:00 Beijing time through the official competition platform.
Choose urban, suburban, or rural living and design a relevant, self-sufficient, low-carbon community, integrating passive energy technologies and sustainable materials into the architecture.
Prepare and submit your design before October 10, 2026 at 24:00 Beijing time, following the submission format in the competition brief.
The jury reviews submissions in November 2026. Winners and honorable mentions are announced with certificates, and advisors of winning projects also receive certificates.
